plainLanguage: Houston has no zoning, so there is no district to pick. Instead, Chapter 42 sets 'building lines' - usually 20 ft from the front property line on a neighborhood street (25 ft on a big road); on many newer small-lot plats the house can sit 10 ft back but a street-facing garage must be about 19-20 ft back. There are no city side or rear setbacks, but fire-safety rules apply within 5 ft of a lot line. Your deed restrictions or HOA rules often add setbacks, masonry or height limits, and the City itself enforces them - check your deed before designing. If your lot is in the 100- or 500-year floodplain, the first floor must be 2 ft above the 500-year flood level. Houston uses the 2021 IRC with local amendments, the Uniform Plumbing Code, and the 2021 energy code with a required solar-ready roof area. A Texas engineer must seal your foundation design. Expect water and wastewater impact fees of about $4,400 if the City serves your lot.
